comment: Context-free translations of all 37 current PaperInterface rows, including the nine exact proposition specifications; every visible model condition and result clause is retained.

student_gaussian_signal_model.tex_statement: For every finite feature type F and continuous Gaussian population M, the joint population law is a probability measure, its latent-skill marginal is the Gaussian law with mean M.priorMean and variance M.priorVariance, its finite noise-vector law on every product rectangle is the product of the featurewise Gaussian laws with mean zero and variances M.noiseVariance(f), and every observed feature satisfies theta_f(student) = q(student) + epsilon_f(student).

access_action_constraints_and_access_ind.tex_statement: For every finite feature type F, population M, requirement policy r, access status z, feasible action a at z, access event A, and primitive student event B: if z is no-access then a is no-take; a.reportImpliesTake; and the joint population law of A x B equals M.accessLaw(A) times the primitive skill-and-noise law of B.

definition1_hidden_access_optional_sourc.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M, test feature t, and literal hidden-access optional equilibrium E, if E satisfies its optional score-stage reporting best-response condition, then E satisfies the explicit hidden-access optional Definition-1 PBO contract: feasible source-timed actions, the required taking and reporting response conditions, and the actual public/report and no-report posterior-mean equations, with the no-report equation guarded by its attained positive-mass event.

definition1_observed_access_optional_ope.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access mass, test feature t, and observed-access optional positive-mass self-enforcing candidate C, C satisfies the explicit operational optional Definition-1 PBO contract: feasible timed actions, attained-branch weak responses and closure almost everywhere, and actual conditional-mean PBO equations only for positive-mass action events.

definition1_observed_access_report_requi.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access mass, test feature t, and report-required-after-taking positive-mass self-enforcing candidate C, C satisfies the explicit operational report-required Definition-1 contract: feasible pre-score actions, actual report and no-take conditional-mean PBOs on attained branches, and almost-everywhere response and closure obligations without assigning a payoff or PBO to a null branch.

definition1_observed_access_mandatory_pb.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access and no-access mass, and test feature t, there exist a mandatory-given-access equilibrium, an access-side reported-score payoff, and a no-access output such that the mandatory Definition-1 contract holds: feasibility fixes the action to take-and-report exactly for access students and no-take otherwise, the access population takes and reports almost everywhere, and both the all-report access PBO and no-access base-only PBO are actual conditional-mean equations.

voluntary_optional_self_enforcing_candid.tex_statement: For a finite decidable feature type F, population M with positive access mass, and test feature t, an optional positive-mass self-enforcing candidate consists of an observed-access optional refined equilibrium whose report branch has positive mass; conditional on a positive no-report branch it supplies integrability of the best continuation payoff, almost-everywhere weak response inequalities for reporters, withholders, takers, and no-takers, and closure against strict profitable entry. It supplies no PBO or payoff assertion for an unattained no-report branch.

voluntary_report_required_self_enforcing.tex_statement: For a finite decidable feature type F, population M with positive access mass, and test feature t, a report-required positive-mass self-enforcing candidate consists of a pre-score take-decision equilibrium and its positive-branch source PBO, has a positive take branch, and, conditional on a positive no-take branch, gives almost-everywhere weak response and strict-gain closure inequalities for takers and no-takers. It does not totalize the no-take payoff when that branch has zero mass.

voluntary_optional_active_branch_selecti.tex_statement: For a finite decidable feature type F, population M with positive access mass, test feature t, and selected optional refined equilibrium E, an optional fibrewise active-branch selection means that E is represented by an optional positive-mass self-enforcing candidate and that on every measurable public-base region of positive population mass, no such candidate can strictly extend E's full take-and-report branch almost everywhere in the branch-extension order.

voluntary_report_required_active_branch_.tex_statement: For a finite decidable feature type F, population M with positive access mass, test feature t, selected report-required take-decision equilibrium E, and its positive-branch source PBO, a report-required fibrewise active-branch selection means that E is represented by a report-required positive-mass self-enforcing candidate and that on every measurable public-base region of positive population mass, no such candidate can strictly extend E's take branch almost everywhere.

observed_access_gaussian_source.tex_statement: An observed-access Gaussian source over a finite decidable feature type F consists of a continuous Gaussian population M, a designated test feature t, positive access probability, positive prior variance, positive variance for every non-test noise coordinate, and positive variance for the test-noise coordinate.

optional_active_branch_profile.tex_statement: For an observed-access Gaussian source S, an optional active-branch profile consists of an observed-access optional positive-mass refined equilibrium for S and an optional fibrewise active-branch selection for that same equilibrium.

report_required_active_branch_profile.tex_statement: For an observed-access Gaussian source S, a report-required active-branch profile consists of a report-required take-decision equilibrium, a positive-branch refined source PBO for that equilibrium under S's access population, and a report-required fibrewise active-branch selection coupled to that PBO.

definition2_latent_skill_fair.tex_statement: For every law-valued policy surface S, latent-skill fairness means that for every equilibrium e, latent skill q, and base feature b, S.latentAccessLaw(e,q,b) = S.latentNoAccessLaw(e,q,b).

definition3_observable_fair.tex_statement: For every law-valued policy surface S, observable fairness means that for every equilibrium e and base feature b, S.observableAccessLaw(e,b) = S.observableNoAccessLaw(e,b).

definition4_demographic_fair.tex_statement: For every law-valued policy surface S, demographic fairness means that for every equilibrium e, S.demographicAccessLaw(e) = S.demographicNoAccessLaw(e).

definition5_test_blank.tex_statement: For every law-valued policy surface S, test blankness means that for every equilibrium e, base feature b, and test value x, S.baseOnlyLaw(e,b) = S.fullFeatureLaw(e,b,x).

fairness_implication_chain.tex_statement: For measurable skill, base, and estimate spaces, a law-valued policy surface S, a conditional skill kernel k, base law nu, latent-law kernels, and observable-law kernels, suppose the latent access and no-access laws are the displayed kernels, each observable law is the bind of k(b) with its corresponding latent kernel, each observable kernel realizes its corresponding observable law, and each demographic law is the bind of nu with its corresponding observable kernel. Then latent-skill fairness of S implies observable fairness of S, and observable fairness of S implies demographic fairness of S.

theorem3_1_optional_reporting_source_tim.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access and no-access mass, test feature t, strictly positive prior and feature-noise variances, probability base law nu, measurable base mean m, positive base variance v, and Gaussian factorization of the hidden-access base-score-skill law, every literal optional hidden-access equilibrium E satisfying its score-stage reporting best response and local positive-mass candidate-entry stability has: zero mass of access no-takers; almost everywhere under the access base-score law, reporting exactly when the displayed finite affine Gaussian-posterior cutoff is met; and strictly positive mass of access no-reporters.

For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access and no-access mass, test feature t, strictly positive prior and feature-noise variances, probability base law nu, measurable base mean m, positive base variance v, and Gaussian factorization of the hidden-access base-score-skill law, every literal optional hidden-access equilibrium E satisfying its score-stage reporting best response and local positive-mass candidate-entry stability has: zero mass of access no-takers; almost everywhere under the access base-score law, reporting exactly when the displayed finite affine Gaussian-posterior cutoff is met; and strictly positive mass of access no-reporters.

theorem3_1_report_required_source_timedS.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M, test feature t, literal report-required hidden-access equilibrium E, positive no-access mass, local-tail-entry stability of E's take rule, strictly positive prior and feature-noise variances, probability base law nu, measurable base mean m, positive base variance v, and Gaussian factorization of the hidden-access base-score-skill law, the access no-report event has positive mass and, for nu-almost every public base value, there is a finite latent-skill cutoff c such that E takes exactly when c <= latentSkill for almost every draw from the corresponding Gaussian location kernel.

theorem3_1_report_required_source_timed.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M, test feature t, literal report-required hidden-access equilibrium E, positive no-access mass, local-tail-entry stability of E's take rule, strictly positive prior and feature-noise variances, probability base law nu, measurable base mean m, positive base variance v, and Gaussian factorization of the hidden-access base-score-skill law, the access no-report event has positive mass and, for nu-almost every public base value, there is a finite latent-skill cutoff c such that E takes exactly when c <= latentSkill for almost every draw from the corresponding Gaussian location kernel.

theorem3_1_hidden_access_pbo_fails_all_f.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access and no-access mass, test feature t, strictly positive prior and noise variances, probability base law nu, measurable base mean m, positive base variance v, and Gaussian factorization, every literal optional equilibrium satisfying its reporting best response and local-candidate stability and every literal report-required equilibrium satisfying local-tail-entry stability induce their respective actual public-output law surfaces, each of which is neither latent-skill fair, observably fair, nor demographically fair.

For every finite decidable feature type F, continuous Gaussian population M with positive access and no-access mass, test feature t, strictly positive prior and noise variances, probability base law nu, measurable base mean m, positive base variance v, and Gaussian factorization, every literal optional equilibrium satisfying its reporting best response and local-candidate stability and every literal report-required equilibrium satisfying local-tail-entry stability induce their respective actual public-output law surfaces, each of which is neither latent-skill fair, observably fair, nor demographically fair.

theorem3_2_optional_reporting_clarified_.tex_statement: For every measurable base space and clarified optional-reporting model C, if C's optional policy is latent-skill fair or observably fair, then for every policy equilibrium e and base value b the score law, base-only law, reporter set, deterministic reported-score output, and measurable deterministic reporter kernel of C satisfy LG21OptionalOperationalTestBlank. The no-report base-only law remains arbitrary within C; the conclusion is the operational zero-reporter-or-almost-everywhere realized-kernel equality notion, not the archival unrestricted randomized-policy statement.

For every measurable base space and clarified optional-reporting model C, if C's optional policy is latent-skill fair or observably fair, then for every policy equilibrium e and base value b the score law, base-only law, reporter set, deterministic reported-score output, and measurable deterministic reporter kernel of C satisfy LG21OptionalOperationalTestBlank. The no-report base-only law remains arbitrary within C; the conclusion is the operational zero-reporter-or-almost-everywhere realized-kernel equality notion, not the archival unrestricted randomized-policy statement.

theorem3_2_report_required_clarified_mod.tex_statement: For every measurable base space and clarified report-required model C, if C's report-required policy is latent-skill fair or observably fair, then for every policy equilibrium e and base value b, C.reportRequired.operationalTestBlank(e,b) holds. The clarified model fixes deterministic reported-score output while allowing the common no-take law to be arbitrary and includes the Gaussian nondegeneracy and finite-expectation conditions needed for its operational almost-everywhere blankness conclusion.

For every measurable base space and clarified report-required model C, if C's report-required policy is latent-skill fair or observably fair, then for every policy equilibrium e and base value b, C.reportRequired.operationalTestBlank(e,b) holds. The clarified model fixes deterministic reported-score output while allowing the common no-take law to be arbitrary and includes the Gaussian nondegeneracy and finite-expectation conditions needed for its operational almost-everywhere blankness conclusion.

lemma4_1_observed_access_strategy_proofn.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F and observed-access Gaussian source S: every mandatory-given-access literal equilibrium takes and reports almost everywhere under S's access population; every optional active-branch profile takes and reports almost everywhere; every report-required active-branch profile takes almost everywhere; and any two profiles of the same voluntary regime agree almost everywhere on the relevant take and report decisions.

For every finite decidable feature type F and observed-access Gaussian source S: every mandatory-given-access literal equilibrium takes and reports almost everywhere under S's access population; every optional active-branch profile takes and reports almost everywhere; every report-required active-branch profile takes almost everywhere; and any two profiles of the same voluntary regime agree almost everywhere on the relevant take and report decisions.

proposition4_2_all_observed_access_requi.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, and Markov no-access estimate kernel K from non-test features to estimates: every optional active-branch profile has its canonical-policy witness for failure of latent-skill fairness; every report-required active-branch profile has its canonical-policy witness for failure of latent-skill fairness; and every mandatory-given-access PBO profile has its mandatory canonical-policy witness for failure of latent-skill fairness. The three quantified protocol families are independent and do not require one shared off-path output or profile.

For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, and Markov no-access estimate kernel K from non-test features to estimates: every optional active-branch profile has its canonical-policy witness for failure of latent-skill fairness; every report-required active-branch profile has its canonical-policy witness for failure of latent-skill fairness; and every mandatory-given-access PBO profile has its mandatory canonical-policy witness for failure of latent-skill fairness. The three quantified protocol families are independent and do not require one shared off-path output or profile.

proposition4_3_all_observed_access_requi.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, positive no-access mass, no-access output g, and actual no-access population PBO for g: every optional or report-required active-branch profile's actual access output admits a positive-variance Gaussian base-skill factorization whose two-branch output law is neither observably fair almost everywhere nor demographically fair; and every mandatory-given-access PBO profile, for every supplied mandatory no-report payoff, satisfies the corresponding mandatory fairness-failure certificate.

For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, positive no-access mass, no-access output g, and actual no-access population PBO for g: every optional or report-required active-branch profile's actual access output admits a positive-variance Gaussian base-skill factorization whose two-branch output law is neither observably fair almost everywhere nor demographically fair; and every mandatory-given-access PBO profile, for every supplied mandatory no-report payoff, satisfies the corresponding mandatory fairness-failure certificate.

definition6_observed_access_source_deriv.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, and positive no-access mass, there is a Definition-6 observed-access source witness derived from S: a base-law and conditional Gaussian score factorization, the access posterior-estimate law, the no-access synthetic conditional-score resampling kernel, and the induced observable and demographic law identities are all obtained from the source population rather than assumed as inputs.

theorem4_4_all_observed_access_requireme.tex_statement: For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, and positive no-access mass: every optional or report-required active-branch profile's actual access output together with the Definition-6 no-access Gaussian resampling kernel has a positive-variance base-skill factorization and is observably and demographically fair in LG21ObservedAccessFair; and every mandatory-given-access PBO profile, with every supplied mandatory no-report payoff, has the mandatory resampling-fairness certificate. The protocol instances are separate and no simultaneous voluntary profile or null-branch completion is assumed.

For every finite decidable feature type F, observed-access Gaussian source S, and positive no-access mass: every optional or report-required active-branch profile's actual access output together with the Definition-6 no-access Gaussian resampling kernel has a positive-variance base-skill factorization and is observably and demographically fair in LG21ObservedAccessFair; and every mandatory-given-access PBO profile, with every supplied mandatory no-report payoff, has the mandatory resampling-fairness certificate. The protocol instances are separate and no simultaneous voluntary profile or null-branch completion is assumed.
